channel.description: Latest articles from RIPR - The Public's Radio - WNPN 89.3 FM (thepublicsradio.org)

item.title: ICE deployments created chaos for cities and cost them millions, NPR analysis finds - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Local leaders report already-strapped police departments racked up overtime bills in the millions while others report a multi-million dollar hit to business during the worst ICE surges.

item.title: Denmark holds early elections spurred by Trump's threats to take Greenland - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Denmark's prime minister called early parliamentary elections after gaining a popularity boost from standing up to President Trump over his threat to seize Greenland.

item.title: Airstrikes may have destroyed Iran's last F-14s, ending a long, strange saga - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: The F-14 was made famous in Top Gun. The U.S. sold the planes to Iran in the 1970s, only for the two countries to become enemies. Iran kept its F-14s flying for decades in the face of U.S. sanctions.

item.title: As parents age, their children face hard choices about when to take the car keys - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: States have many policies to stop risky older drivers from renewing their licenses. But in practice, it's often adult children who must decide when to take the car keys away from an aging parent.

item.title: Trump takes aim at windmills despite increasing energy costs - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: President Trump's mission to fight renewable wind energy comes at a time of rising energy costs.

item.title: Trump delivers farmers another financial blow with Iran war - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Some of President Trump's policies, the latest being the war in Iran, are testing his support among farmers who are being burdened with higher costs.

item.title: Kim vows to 'irreversibly' cement North Korea's nuclear status - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: In his speech, Kim expressed pride in the country's rapid expansion of nuclear weapons and missiles in recent years, calling it the "right" choice.

item.title: Iran fires more missiles at Israel, dismisses Trump's talk as 'fake news' - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Israeli health officials said Iranian missiles struck four sites across Israel Tuesday, including central Tel Aviv, injuring at least six people. Iranian authorities also said a gas supply line in southwest Iran was struck overnight.

item.title: Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Pulido has been a mainstay of Tejano music —a genre blending traditional regional Mexican elements with country, pop and conjunto influences — for more than three decades.

item.title: A professional cornhole player and quadruple amputee is arrested for murder - TPR: The Public's Radio
item.description: Dayton Webber, 27, is accused of shooting a man in his car during an argument. He has shared his story of becoming a pro athlete after losing his arms and legs to a childhood bacterial infection.
